title: Searching for Embedded Protoplanets with the Keck/NIRC2 Vortex Coronagraph: Confirmation of a Core-accretion Planet in the Narrow Gap of the Elias 2-24 Disk
question: Assess whether embedded protoplanets in seven young stars hosting protoplanetary disks with substructures (gaps, cavities) can be directly detected with the Keck/NIRC2 vortex coronagraph.

what.value: Stellar distances from Gaia DR3 and Hipparcos, stellar ages, spectral types, and WISE W1/W2 photometry used to estimate L' and Ms magnitudes

evidence.quote: : Keck/NIRC2 Vortex observations. $L'$ magnitudes are estimated via logarithmic interpolation between WISE W1 and W2 bands. The $M_s$ magnitude of PDS 70 is approximated using the WISE W2 band.

what.value: Previous astrometry and L'-band contrast of Elias 2-24 b from VLT/NACO and re-analysis

evidence.quote: (cite: Jorquera2021) reported a separation of $0.411\pm0.008^{\prime\prime}$ and a position angle of $302.1\pm1.1^\circ$ (possibly the uncertainties presented for the astrometric position included only the errors on the fit and are likely underestimated), while (cite: Pinte2023b) derived a separation of $0.37\pm0.04^{\prime\prime}$ and a position angle of $298.4\pm4.6^\circ$.
(cite: Jorquera2021) measured an $L'$-band contrast of $8.81\pm0.12$ mag, while (cite: Pinte2023b) obtained a value of $8.78^{+0.98}_{-0.48}$ mag.

what.value: Disk inclination (23.6 deg), position angle (43.4 deg), stellar mass (0.78 +0.35/-0.13 M_sun), and interstellar extinction (A_V = 8.7 mag, A_L' = 0.5 mag) for Elias 2-24

evidence.quote: Adopting a disk inclination of $23.6^\circ$ and a position angle of $43.4^\circ$ (cite: Cieza2017), together with a stellar mass of $0.78^{+0.35}_{-0.13}$ M~$\odot$~ (cite: Andrews2018), we infer a predicted motion of $6.2^{+2.2}_{-1.1}$$^\circ$.
As reported in (cite: Cieza2021), Elias 2-24 has an extinction of $A_V=8.7$ mag, corresponding to $0.5$ mag in the $L'$ band.

what.value: Hydrodynamical model mass predictions (0.41 and 1.72 M_Jup) for the planet carving the gap in Elias 2-24

evidence.quote: Adopting the mass predictions from the hydrodynamical models of (cite: Zhang2018), we then estimate accretion rates for two masses: 0.41 and 1.72 M~Jup~.

recipe.goal: Pre-process raw Keck/NIRC2 vortex coronagraph frames and subtract stellar PSF via PCA-ADI and RDI
recipe.method: Apply dark-field and flat-field corrections, bad pixel interpolation in a 5x5 box, geometrical distortion correction, PCA-based sky subtraction, image registration via speckle cross-correlation, and stellar PSF removal using annular and full-frame PCA-ADI as well as PCA-RDI and median-filtered de-rotation.
key_parameters: Bad pixel replacement box: 5x5 neighboring box
Annular PCA parameters: 0.2-FWHM parallactic angle threshold, 1-FWHM inner mask, 15-pixel (0.15 arcsec) wide annuli

recipe.goal: Derive astrometry and photometry of detected point sources using NEGFC
recipe.method: Negative Fake Companion (NEGFC) technique using unocculted stellar PSF models to measure separation, position angle, and flux ratio relative to the host star.

recipe.goal: Compute 5-sigma contrast curves and planetary mass detection limits
recipe.method: Compute 5-sigma contrast curves across multiple numbers of PCs taking the deepest contrast at each separation, accounting for small-sample statistics with a t-distribution, and convert contrasts to planet mass limits using evolutionary models.
assumptions: Gaussian noise with t-distribution for small-sample statistics; system ages and distances from Table 1 (1 Myr upper limit for Elias 2-24); ATMO-NEQ-STRONG 2023 models.

recipe.goal: Test common proper motion, background false alarm probability, and orbital motion of Elias 2-24 b
recipe.method: Compare 2018 and 2020 Keck astrometry against static background hypothesis, compute proper-motion False Alarm Probability (FAP) using a synthetic star sample from the Besancon Galaxy Model, and estimate expected Keplerian orbital displacement by 2026.
key_parameters: Besancon query: distances 0-50 kpc, radius 5 arcmin around Elias 2-24, apparent L' = 15-17 mag, FoV = 2.6 arcsec
assumptions: Circular orbit coplanar with the disk (inclination = 23.6 deg, PA = 43.4 deg) and stellar mass = 0.78 +0.35/-0.13 M_sun; interstellar extinction A_V = 8.7 mag.

recipe.goal: Characterize the evolutionary mass, effective temperature, and mass accretion rate of Elias 2-24 b
recipe.method: Convert L' contrast to absolute L' magnitude correcting for distance and extinction, compare with 1 Myr isochrones of ATMO-NEQ-STRONG 2023, AMES-COND, AMES-DUSTY, and BEX (coldest/warm, hot, hottest start) evolutionary models, and interpolate circumplanetary disk accretion models of Zhu (2015).
key_parameters: Inner circumplanetary disk radius: 2 R_Jup; planet masses tested for accretion rate: 0.41, 1.72, and 3.0 M_Jup
assumptions: Age = 1 Myr, distance = 139.3 pc, A_V = 8.7 mag (A_L' = 0.5 mag, equal for star and planet), evolutionary models neglect accretion luminosity.

evidence.quote: In the annular PCA case, the significance exceeds $3\sigma$ for more than 6 subtracted PCs and reaches a maximum of $3.85\sigma$ (SNR of 4.49) for 27 PCs, while the full-frame PCA reduction yield a peak significance of $3.69\sigma$ (SNR of 4.28) for 6 PCs.

evidence.quote: The companion was recovered with a lower significance, peaking at $2.82\sigma$ (SNR of 3.11) for 5 PCs, in the 2020 epoch.

answer_key.quantity: Rejection significance of static background hypothesis for Elias 2-24 b

evidence.quote: The comparison between the expected position of a background source, shown as a blue square, and the position of the candidate, shown as a purple circle, shows that the candidate is incompatible with the static background hypothesis at the 3.2$\sigma$ confidence level.

answer_key.quantity: False alarm probability (FAP) of background star within 2.6 arcsec FoV

evidence.quote: Considering a field of view of $2.6^{\prime\prime}$, we derive a FAP of $1.50\cdot10^{-4}$, corresponding to a $3.6\sigma$ significance.

answer_key.quantity: Absolute L' magnitude of Elias 2-24 b

evidence.quote: Assuming that the star and the planet experience the same extinction, we derive an absolute $L'$ magnitude of $10.08^{+0.53}_{-0.87}$ mag for Elias 2-24 b.
